newsitem.title: UK: Hepworth discusses sale of refractories unit.
newsitem.headline: Hepworth discusses sale of refractories unit.

text.p: British heating and building materials group Hepworth Plc said on Monday it was in talks with a number of parties on the possible sale of its refractories division.
It said in a statement the discussions may or may not lead to sale of the business.
Hepworth reported half year pretax profits of 35.5 million stg, down from 37.5 million stg, on September 27.
The Sunday Telegraph newspaper reported yesterday that Hepworth had put the division up for sale.

The newspaper said trade sources suggested interested parties could include Radex-Heraklith, based in Austria, Global Industrial Technology, Lafarge of France, Cookson and possibly CinVen, the venture capital group.
In another article, the Sunday Telegraph said engineering group Morgan Crucible might also be interested in Hepworth's refractories unit.

Hepworth chief executive John Carter said at the time of interim results that markets had been tough and attributed the group's relatively robust performance to efficiency gains and a focus on international markets.
